lessons.title: Ultimate Konglish Guide
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 134 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: I took a photo with a new smartphone
cards.explanation: Learn this Konglish noun as Korean vocabulary; do not translate it word-for-word.
cards.source_sentence: 새 스마트폰으로 사진을 찍었어요

cards.translation: I ate a sandwich for lunch
cards.explanation: Learn this borrowed noun with its Korean pronunciation and spelling.
cards.source_sentence: 점심으로 샌드위치를 먹었어요

cards.translation: I went to the shopping mall and shopped on the weekend
cards.explanation: Learn this borrowed noun as a fixed Korean word.
cards.source_sentence: 주말에 쇼핑몰에 가서 쇼핑했어요

cards.translation: If you press this button, the screen turns on
cards.explanation: Learn this borrowed noun with the Korean collocation used here.
cards.source_sentence: 이 버튼을 누르면 화면이 켜져요

cards.translation: There are many apartments in this neighborhood
cards.explanation: Learn this Konglish noun as Korean vocabulary.
cards.source_sentence: 이 동네에는 아파트가 많아요

lessons.meaning: Konglish consists of Korean words borrowed or adapted from English and used with Korean pronunciation and meaning.
lessons.when_to_use: Use these familiar-looking words carefully: their Korean meaning, pronunciation and usage may differ from English.
lessons.how_to_build: There is no single grammar rule. Learn each Konglish item as Korean vocabulary and follow the source examples for spelling and collocation.
examples: 스마트폰
smart phone
샌드위치
sandwich
쇼핑몰
shopping mall
버튼
button
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: Different meanings of 성
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 135 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: There is a high possibility that it will rain tomorrow
cards.explanation: Choose the noun ending in 성 that expresses possibility.
cards.source_sentence: 내일 비가 올 가능성이 높아요

cards.translation: That person's words always lack sincerity
cards.explanation: Choose the noun ending in 성 that expresses sincerity or truthfulness.
cards.source_sentence: 그 사람의 말은 항상 진실성이 부족해요

cards.prompt: 이 사건과 저 사건의 ___ 아예 없어요
cards.translation: There is no relevance between these incidents
cards.explanation: Choose the noun ending in 성 that expresses relevance.
cards.source_sentence: 이 사건과 저 사건의 관련성이 아예 없어요

cards.translation: That child's creativity is outstanding
cards.explanation: Choose the noun ending in 성 that expresses creativity.
cards.source_sentence: 그 아이의 창의성은 매우 뛰어나요

cards.prompt: 세상에는 아직도 ___ 인권이 매우 낮은 곳이 많습니다
cards.translation: There are still many places where women's rights are very low
cards.explanation: Recognize 여성 as a noun with a different meaning from the productive 성 ending.
cards.source_sentence: 세상에는 아직도 여성의 인권이 매우 낮은 곳이 많습니다

lessons.meaning: 성 has several meanings and readings depending on the Hanja-based word in which it appears.
lessons.when_to_use: Use context and the complete word to distinguish the meanings introduced by HTSK.
lessons.how_to_build: This is vocabulary rather than one ending; learn 성 compounds and their pronunciation and meanings as listed on the official page.
examples: 내일 비가 올 가능성이 높아요
There is a high possibility that it will rain tomorrow
그 사람의 말은 항상 진실성이 부족해요
That person's words always lack sincerity
이 사건과 저 사건의 관련성이 아예 없어요
There is absolutely no relevance between this incident and that one
그 아이의 창의성은 매우 뛰어나요
That child's creativity is outstanding

lessons.title: Because with ~기에 and ~길래
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 136 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Beef was on sale at the supermarket, so I bought a lot of it
cards.explanation:
~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.

Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.

Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
cards.source_sentence: 소고기가 마트에서 할인하기에 많이 사 왔어요

cards.translation: That girl was very pretty, so I asked for her number
cards.explanation:
~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.

Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.

Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
cards.source_sentence: 그 여자가 너무 예쁘기에 전화번호를 물어봤어요

cards.prompt: 자연분만이 제왕절개보다 회복이 ___ 이번에도 자연분만하기로 했어요
cards.translation: The recovery of a natural birth is faster than a C-section, so this time as well, I have decided to give birth naturally
cards.explanation:
~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.

Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.

Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
cards.source_sentence: 자연분만이 제왕절개보다 회복이 빠르길래 이번에도 자연분만하기로 했어요

cards.prompt: 친구가 자연분만을 했는데 제왕절개보다 회복이 빠르다고 ___ 저도 자연분만을 할 거예요
cards.translation: My friend said that the recovery of a natural birth is faster than a c-section, so I too will give birth naturally
cards.explanation:
~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.

Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.

Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
cards.source_sentence: 친구가 자연분만을 했는데 제왕절개보다 회복이 빠르다고 하길래 저도 자연분만을 할 거예요

cards.translation: They say that the flu shot is a necessity, so I also got it
cards.explanation:
~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.

Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.

Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
cards.source_sentence: 독감주사가 필수라고 하길래 저도 맞았어요

lessons.meaning: ~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.
lessons.when_to_use: Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
examples: 소고기가 마트에서 할인하길래 많이 사 왔어요
Beef was on sale at the supermarket, so I bought a lot
그 여자가 너무 예쁘길래 전화번호를 물어봤어요
That woman was so pretty that I asked for her phone number
양반다리를 하고 앉길래 당신의 자세가 불편하다고 생각했어요

lessons.title: Necessity with ~아/어야
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 137 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Kimchi must be made at home/with one’s own hands for it to be delicious
cards.explanation:
~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.

Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.

Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
cards.source_sentence: 김치는 손수 만들어야 맛있어요

cards.translation: Only if fish is raw is it delicious
cards.explanation:
~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.

Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.

Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
cards.source_sentence: 생선이 날것이어야 맛있어요

cards.translation: Only if you put the bill in upside down does it go in
cards.explanation:
~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.

Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.

Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
cards.source_sentence: 지폐를 거꾸로 넣어야 들어가요

cards.translation: Only if you open the window will the room be well ventilated
cards.explanation:
~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.

Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.

Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
cards.source_sentence: 창문을 열어야 방에 환기가 잘 돼요

cards.translation: Only if you put lemon in food does the sour taste come out (does it taste sour)
cards.explanation:
~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.

Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.

Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
cards.source_sentence: 음식에 레몬을 넣어야 신맛이 나요

lessons.meaning: ~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
examples: 사람들은 물을 마셔야 살아요
People must drink water to live
그래야 맛있어요

lessons.title: Should have with ~았/었어야 하다
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 138 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: I should have checked the calorie indicator before I ate it all
cards.explanation:
~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.

Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.

Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
cards.source_sentence: 다 먹기 전에 열량 표시를 확인했었어야 해요

cards.translation: This creation should have been displayed before the artist passed away
cards.explanation:
~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.

Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.

Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
cards.source_sentence: 이 작품은 화가가 죽기 전에 출시됐어야 해요

cards.prompt: 이 그림들을 곧 전시할 거라서 액자에 ___
cards.translation: I’m going to display these paintings soon, so I need to put them into frames
cards.explanation:
~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.

Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.

Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
cards.source_sentence: 이 그림들을 곧 전시할 거라서 액자에 넣어야 해요

cards.translation: I had to put them in frames
cards.explanation:
~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.

Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.

Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
cards.source_sentence: 액자에 넣어야 했어요

cards.translation: Instead of tap water, you need to put in mineral water
cards.explanation:
~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.

Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.

Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
cards.source_sentence: 수돗물 대신에 생수를 넣어야 돼

lessons.meaning: ~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.
lessons.how_to_build: Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
examples: 달빛이 예뻐서 사진을 찍었어야 해요
The moonlight was beautiful; I should have taken a picture
몸살이 나기 전에 병원에 갔어야 해요
You should have gone to the hospital before your body started aching
수돗물 말고 애기한테 생수를 먹였어야 해요
You should have given the baby mineral water instead of tap water

lessons.title: It was okay to with ~았/었어도 되다
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 139 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: You could have taken a tray
cards.explanation:
~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.

Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.

Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
cards.source_sentence: 쟁반을 가져갔어도 돼요

cards.translation: There is no money in that account at all, so you could have closed it
cards.explanation:
~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.

Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.

Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
cards.source_sentence: 그 계좌에 돈이 아예 없어서 해지했어도 돼요

cards.prompt: 여기에 아무 것도 없을 거라서 기둥을 ___
cards.translation: There won’t be anything here, so you could have erected a pillar here
cards.explanation:
~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.

Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.

Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
cards.source_sentence: 여기에 아무 것도 없을 거라서 기둥을 세웠어도 돼요

cards.prompt: 현혈하는 것이 위험한 수술이 아니라서 오기 전에 아무거나 ___
cards.translation: Giving blood is not a dangerous surgery, so you could have eaten anything before you came
cards.explanation:
~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.

Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.

Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
cards.source_sentence: 현혈하는 것이 위험한 수술이 아니라서 오기 전에 아무거나 먹었어도 돼요

cards.prompt: 이 야채에 살충제를 안 뿌려서 안 ___
cards.translation: There isn’t/wasn’t pesticides sprayed on these vegetables, so you don’t need to wash them
cards.explanation:
~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.

Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.

Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
cards.source_sentence: 이 야채에 살충제를 안 뿌려서 안 씻어도 돼요

lessons.source_title: It was okay to with ~았/었어도 되다
lessons.meaning: ~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
examples: 제비뽑기를 해서 일을 맡기는 것 대신에 그냥 저한테 맡겼어도 돼요

언론사가 대통령을 인터뷰했어도 됐어요

lessons.title: As a role with ~(으)로서
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 140 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.prompt: ___ 가족을 책임져야 하기 때문에 어깨가 무겁다
cards.translation: There is a lot of burden on the breadwinner because he/she is responsible for the family
cards.explanation:
~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.

Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.

Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
cards.source_sentence: 가장으로서 가족을 책임져야 하기 때문에 어깨가 무겁다

cards.prompt: 그 선수는 우리 팀의 ___ 경기를 이끌고 있어요
cards.translation: That player is leading the game as the captain of our team
cards.explanation:
~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.

Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.

Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
cards.source_sentence: 그 선수는 우리 팀의 주장으로서 경기를 이끌고 있어요

cards.prompt: ___ 해야 할 일이 너무 많아서 때로는 힘들다
cards.translation: As a mom, there are many things that I have to do, so it is difficult sometimes
cards.explanation:
~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.

Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.

Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
cards.source_sentence: 엄마로서 해야 할 일이 너무 많아서 때로는 힘들다

cards.prompt: 저는 그 사건의 ___ 재판을 전담하기로 했습니다
cards.translation: I decided to take full charge of that court case as the prosecutor
cards.explanation:
~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.

Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.

Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
cards.source_sentence: 저는 그 사건의 검사로서 재판을 전담하기로 했습니다

cards.translation: Seulgi played a big active role in the playoffs as the captain/leader of the soccer team
cards.explanation:
~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.

Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.

Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
cards.source_sentence: 슬기는 축구팀의 주장으로서 결승전에서 큰 활약을 했다

lessons.meaning: ~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
examples: 그 사람은 운동선수로서 한국에서 유명하다
That person is famous as an athlete in Korea
그 사람은 하버드 대학의 졸업생으로서 제일 똑똑한 학생 중 한 명이었다
That person was known as one of the smartest graduates of Harvard University
엄마로서의 삶은 내가 생각한 것보다 훨씬 어려웠다
Life as a mom was much more difficult than I thought
저의 새 언니가 아내로서는 좋지만 엄마로서는 별로예요

lessons.title: By means of with ~(으)로써
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 141 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Coffee is made using roasted beans
cards.explanation:
~(으)로써 means by means of, through or by using something.

Use it to name the method, tool or means by which an action is accomplished.

Attach ~로써 after a vowel and ~으로써 after a consonant; place it after the noun representing the means.
cards.source_sentence: 커피는 볶은 콩으로써 만들어진다

cards.translation: I put the nail in the wall using a thick piece of wood
cards.explanation:
~(으)로써 means by means of, through or by using something.

Use it to name the method, tool or means by which an action is accomplished.

Attach ~로써 after a vowel and ~으로써 after a consonant; place it after the noun representing the means.
cards.source_sentence: 저는 굵은 나무로써 벽에 못을 박았어요

cards.prompt: 오늘 밤에 있는 경기는 ___ 치열한 경기가 될 것이다
cards.translation: The match tonight will be a fierce revenge match
cards.explanation:

cards.explanation:
HTSK uses ~ㄴ/는다니, ~다니 and related forms to react to information with surprise, displeasure or astonishment. The speaker responds to something just said and adds an emotional attitude.

Use this ending as a short conversational reaction when the previous statement is surprising, unbelievable or displeasing. The exact feeling comes from the context and intonation.

Use the plain form followed by 니: 가다 → 간다니, 먹다 → 먹는다니, 먹었다 → 먹었다니, 행복하다 → 행복하다니. With nouns use ~(이)라니; replace 고 in quoted suggestions, questions or commands with 니: 가자니, 가느냐니, 가라니.

lessons.title: Because of being busy with ~느라고

~느라고 gives a reason based on being occupied with one action, usually with a negative or inconvenient result.

Use it when one activity prevents, delays or causes difficulty for another action.

Attach ~느라고 to a verb stem; the subject and tense restrictions and the negative-result nuance are important in HTSK.

cards.translation: All the members of my family are spread apart, so nobody was able to contact anybody
cards.explanation:

cards.prompt: 불현듯 과거의 나쁜 기억이 떠오르면 일부러 신나는 음악을 ___

cards.explanation:
~고는 하다 and the contracted ~곤 하다 describe a habitual or repeated action, often in the past.

Use them for things someone regularly used to do or would often do.

Attach ~고는 하다 to the verb and contract it to ~곤 하다 in speech; conjugate 하다 for tense and politeness.

cards.explanation: Use the adverb for an especially unfortunate or ironic coincidence.

lessons.source_title: Unfortunately / of all things with 하필
lessons.meaning: 하필 means unfortunately, of all things or at the worst possible choice/time.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it to highlight an especially unlucky, unexpected or inconvenient selection.
lessons.how_to_build: Place 하필 before the word or clause being singled out; it is an adverb and does not take a productive ending.
examples: 하필 밥을 다 차리고 먹기 전에 전화가 와서 통화하는 바람에 밥이 다 식었어
I got all of the food ready and right before I was about to eat, of all things, the phone rang and because I was talking on the phone, the food got all cold
된장국을 끓이려고 감자를 샀는데 하필 뜨거운 전자레인지 위에 올려놓아서 감자가 다 썩었어
I bought potatoes so I could boil up some bean-paste soup, but of all places, I put the potatoes on top of the microwave and they got hot and rotted
얼렁뚱땅 거짓말을 하고 넘어가려고 했는데 하필 같이 있던 친구가 사실을 말하는 바람에 난감해졌어
I told a lie and wanted to just go past it but, of all people, one of my friends who was there told everybody the truth so I got really embarrassed
좋은 자리에서 공연을 보려고 사람들을 비집고 자리를 잡았는데 하필 내가 싫어하는 사람 옆에 서서 공연을 보게 됐어

lessons.title: As expected with 어쩐지
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 150 focus. Use the official Unit 6 lesson for the full explanation.

cards.translation: No wonder they have so much money
cards.explanation: Use the adverb when a later fact explains an earlier impression.
cards.source_sentence: 어쩐지 돈이 많아요

cards.translation: They are a dual-income couple, so no wonder they have money
cards.explanation: Use the adverb when a later fact explains an earlier impression.
cards.source_sentence: 맞벌이 부부라서 어쩐지 돈이 많아요

cards.translation: No wonder the bed was uncomfortable
cards.explanation: Use the adverb when a later fact explains an earlier impression.
cards.source_sentence: 어쩐지 침대가 불편했어요

cards.explanation: Use the adverb when a later fact explains an earlier impression.

cards.explanation: Use the adverb when a later fact explains an earlier impression.

lessons.meaning: 어쩐지 means no wonder, as expected or somehow, connecting a new realization with a reason or intuition.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when a result now makes sense or when the speaker had a vague feeling about it.
lessons.how_to_build: Place 어쩐지 before the clause and conjugate the rest normally; learn the discourse use from HTSK examples.
examples: 어쩐지 그 아이가 음식만 보면 바로 집어삼켰어요
No wonder that baby devoured his food at the very sight of it

No wonder that baby devoured his food at the very sight of it, I thought there was something wrong with his personality
어쩐지 그 사람이 야구를 하는 게 어색해 보였어요
No wonder that person looks strange playing baseball
어쩐지 그 사람이 왼손잡이를 위해 만들어진 글러브를 끼고 야구를 하는 게 어색해 보였어요
That person wore gloves made for a left-handed person, so no wonder he looked so strange playing baseball
